plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: An epiphytic cactus with flat, segmented, scalloped stems and arching, zygomorphic flowers. Widely grown as a houseplant, it flowers in response to shorter days and cool nights.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (November–January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to the coastal mountains of southeastern Brazil; cultivated worldwide as a houseplant
plants.funFact: Unlike desert cacti, it grows on trees in humid Brazilian forests, and it can be told apart from the Christmas cactus by the pointed teeth on its stem segments.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves and large panicles of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers that carpet streets and gardens when they fall.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October–December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In parts of Australia, jacaranda bloom coincides with university exams, and students traditionally joke that if a flower falls on your head you will pass.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and slightly fragrant, delicate single or semi-double flowers. It is among the earliest camellias to bloom and thrives in mild climates.
plants.location: Native to Japan and southern China; cultivated across the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Oil pressed from sasanqua seeds is used in Japan for cooking and cosmetics, and its leaves can be used to make a tea.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose showy colored bracts, which are modified leaves, surround small yellow true flowers called cyathia. Outdoors in warm climates it forms large shrubs, while elsewhere it is a popular potted holiday plant.
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in subtropical regions and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias need long nights of about 12 hours or more for several weeks to develop colored bracts, and in the wild they can grow up to 4 meters tall.
